story: I paid Rs 5,00,000 to an interior designer in Pune on 1 July 2026; work never started and no refund.

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 01 Jul 2028 (601 days left). This counts 2 years from 01 Jul 2026 (your purchase date - counted from the earliest possible day, to be safe). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.

facts_used.start_basis: purchase date (earliest possible start, to be safe)

rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 500,000, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with no filing fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

answer.summary: You paid Rs 5,00,000 to an interior designer in Pune for work that never started. You can file a consumer complaint for a refund. Since you paid Rs 5,00,000, you must file at the District Consumer Commission, and there is no filing fee.

claims.text: You are a consumer because you bought a service for Rs 5,00,000 to use for your personal home, not for business.
Refusing to refund money for work that never started is an unfair trade practice.
The complaint must be filed within two years from 1 July 2026, so before 1 July 2028.
You must file at the District Consumer Commission because the amount paid is Rs 5,00,000, which is up to Rs 50,00,000.
There is no filing fee for your complaint.

next_steps.action: Gather your proof of payment, like bank transfer details or receipts.
next_steps.why: You need to show you paid Rs 5,00,000.

next_steps.action: Send a written refund request to the interior designer or their grievance officer.
next_steps.why: This is a free first step that can solve the problem without going to court.

next_steps.action: Call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
next_steps.why: They can help you get a refund for free.

next_steps.action: File your complaint online at e-jagriti.gov.in or in person at the District Consumer Commission in Pune.
next_steps.why: This starts the official legal process to get your Rs 5,00,000 back.

support.text: You are a consumer because you bought a service for Rs 5,00,000 to use for your personal home, not for business.
support.reason: The law text defines 'consumer' as a person who hires or avails of any service for consideration, and explicitly excludes a person who avails of such service for any commercial purpose. The sentence states the service was for personal home use, not for business, which directly fits the definition and the non-commercial purpose exclusion.

support.text: Refusing to refund money for work that never started is an unfair trade practice.
support.reason: The law text explicitly lists 'refusing, after selling goods or rendering services, to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof' as an unfair trade practice. The sentence describes refusing to refund money for work that never started, which is a deficient service, and this matches the law text.

support.text: The complaint must be filed within two years from 1 July 2026, so before 1 July 2028.
support.reason: The law text states complaints must be filed within two years from the date the cause of action arose. The sentence computes the deadline as 1 July 2028, which is correct based on the 1 July 2026 date given (two years later), so the legal rule is supported.

support.text: You must file at the District Consumer Commission because the amount paid is Rs 5,00,000, which is up to Rs 50,00,000.
support.reason: The law text states District Commission has jurisdiction for consideration paid up to Rs 50 lakh. The sentence states the amount is Rs 5,00,000, which is up to Rs 50,00,000, so the legal rule about jurisdiction is supported.

support.text: You must file at the District Consumer Commission because the amount paid is Rs 5,00,000, which is up to Rs 50,00,000.
support.reason: The law text [CPA2019_s34_2] provides jurisdictional rules based on where the opposite party resides, carries on business, or where the cause of action arises - it does NOT provide any pecuniary jurisdiction limits. The sentence incorrectly applies a Rs 50 lakh limit to the District Commission, which is not in this law text. The pecuniary limit is in a different law text [CPJR2021_pecuniary].

support.text: There is no filing fee for your complaint.
support.reason: The law text [CPFEE_r7] explicitly states 'No fee where the consideration paid is up to Rs 5 lakh.' The sentence states the consideration paid is Rs 5,00,000, which is up to Rs 5 lakh, so there is no filing fee - this directly matches the law text.

Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for refund

On 01 July 2026 I paid Rs 500,000 to you for [FILL: product/service and order number]. [FILL: what went wrong, e.g. product defective / service not provided]. Despite my requests you have not refunded the amount.

I request a full refund of Rs 500,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If the refund is not made, I intend to file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
